ctx.x: So then guys are -- the whole trip was like that. It's just one thing after another. The only thing that was fairly calm was the 4th of July. We were invited to the Embassy for the 4th of July party and that morning all of the Russians very seriously came up and shook my hand to say congratulations on the anniversary of your revolution. I said, "That's right, it was a revolution."

And I see a crowd of people and Benny says, "Come over here." I came over and there's a little fat guy standing there. Benny says, "Meet Premier Krushchev." So I pull out my Russian and say (RUSSIAN), "I'm glad to meet you." And Krushchev said, in Russian, you speak very good Russian. Then he said something I couldn't understand and everybody laughed. He said, "You're the only American he's ever been afraid of." I said, "Why?" He says, "Bolshoi". I just towered over him, he came below my belly. He said I was the…
That American image is quite cheesy(?) in Moscow, isn't it?
